subject: Post-call: regional quality triage & pilot checklist
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Thomas Berg <thomas.berg@globeco.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-08T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: regional quality triage & pilot checklist

Hi Thomas — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick written recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned.

Call highlights (short):
- Primary goals: improve customer support triage in FR/DE/ES (EU) and QA/autoresponder accuracy for JA/KO (APAC).
- Volume: ~6k monthly end-user messages; expected 2x growth during peak months.
- Key constraints: low latency for chat flows (<250ms p95 target), strict PII retention policies, and conservative hallucination tolerances for transactional replies.

Initial model-fit recommendations (for pilot):
- EU (FR/DE/ES): redwood-intl-7b-qa (FP16/8-bit quantized) — balances cost & multilingual quality.
- APAC (JA/KO): redwood-reason-2.7b-intl with aggressive prompt engineering and localized tokenization; fallback to redwood-13b-lite if kernel/latency shows issues.
- For high-precision tasks (legal templating): run a reranker pass using redwood-rerank-1b.

Benchmarks & artifacts attached / links:
- Attached: regional-benchmark-summary.xlsx (high-level pass/fail vs your sample prompts)
- Prompt sets and starter evaluation harness: prompt-sets-fr-de-ja.yml (Drive link included below)
- Baseline cadence: 2-week pilot, automated evals nightly, manual triage weekly.

Primary risks we flagged on the call:
- Quality regressions when we quantize aggressively for latency. We'll supply paired evals (float32 vs quantized) and a rollback policy.
- Japanese tokenization edge cases for domain-specific terms — we recommend a small tokenization override map during the pilot.

Proposed next steps (can we lock these by EOD Friday?):
1) You confirm languages & three priority intents for pilot (e.g., billing, order status, return).
2) We provision a 2-week hosted pilot (no infra commitment) and share nightly eval dashboards.
3) We share prompt-set + baseline runs and a short task-specific scoring rubric for your QA team.
4) Sign pilot-scope-template.docx (I attached a draft) — we can update hours & SLOs after kickoff.

Drive links: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1aB-RegionalBenchmark2027
HubSpot deal (we'll create): HB-4482 — I will loop Neha for architecture and Aditya for pricing.

Thanks — I’ll schedule a short kickoff once you confirm scope.

—
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0198

Attachments (referenced): regional-benchmark-summary.xlsx, prompt-sets-fr-de-ja.yml, pilot-scope-template.docx

Subject: Re: Post-call: regional quality triage & pilot checklist

Thanks Marissa — this looks good. A few quick clarifications from my side:

- We can confirm FR/DE/ES + JA/KO as the initial set. Priority intents: order status (P1), billing inquiries (P2), password resets/account lockouts (P3).
- Latency: p95 should ideally be <300ms for our in-chat flows; we understand tradeoffs with quantization.
- Hallucination: for billing and password-reset flows we need extremely conservative generation (prefer fail-closed).

Could you share: 1) a small example prompt set for JA that demonstrates tokenization overrides; 2) sample eval output (precision/recall/confidence) for the redwood-intl-7b-qa vs the quantized variant so we can review with our SREs?

Assuming those are acceptable, we are happy to run the 2-week hosted pilot. We need a short checklist for our procurement and legal to expedite the signature.

—
Thomas Berg
Head of Product — International Support | GlobalCo
thomas.berg@globeco.com
